item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
400
ABNT20 KNHC 261157
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM EDT Sat Sep 26 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Gonzalo, located just east-northeast of the Cabo Verde
Islands, and on Tropical Depression Fay, located well to the
west-southwest of the Azores.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Katz

----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...29.6N 44.0W
ABOUT 1130 MI...1820 KM WSW OF THE AZORES

PRESENT MOVEMENT...WSW OR 240 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1009 MB...29.80 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM GMT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Fay was
located near latitude 29.6 North, longitude 44.0 West. The
depression is moving toward the west-southwest near 5 mph (7 km/h). 
A more southerly turn and an increase in forward speed is expected 
to occur over the next few days. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast over the next several days.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1009 mb (29.80 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Papin

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Forecast Discussion Number 26
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM GMT Sat Sep 26 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 261438
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Depression Fay Discussion Number  26
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 PM GMT Sat Sep 26 2026
 
Fay has not changed significantly since the previous update. The 
tropical cyclone is clearly still being impacted by both wind shear 
and dry air. The most recent TAFB Dvorak intensity estimate was 
T2.0/30 kt, and the objective intensity estimate is in the range of 
31-41 kt. Therefore, the initial intensity has been held at 30 kt 
for this advisory.  

The cyclone continues to drift towards the west-southwest, at  250/4 
kt. A more southerly turn is expected as Fay continues move into the 
southern flank of the subtropical Atlantic high. By early next week, 
most of the guidance has the depression turning westward due to the 
large-scale easterly flow. However there is a bit of uncertainty in 
the precise timing of this turn. The current NHC forecast track is 
similar to the previous one with some minor adjustments based on the 
HCCA forecast aid. 

There is a high level of uncertainty in the intensity forecast as 
Fay remains over an area of favorably warm sea-surface temperatures, 
but vertical wind shear and dry mid-level air will likely continue 
to hinder the system, preventing a more organized structure from 
developing. Convection is likely to continue pulsing but the current 
NHC intensity forecast follows the trend of the previous one showing 
little change in strength with only minor adjustments made. This 
forecast continues to maintain Fay as a tropical depression until it 
becomes post-tropical and dissipates by the middle of next week.

item.title: Tropical Storm Gonzalo Public Advisory Number 6
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026 
000
WTNT32 KNHC 260847
TCPAT2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Gonzalo Advisory Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL072026
800 AM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026
 
...GONZALO STILL A TROPICAL STORM AS IT MOVES AWAY FROM THE CABO 
VERDE ISLANDS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM CVT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.6N 23.0W
ABOUT 60 MI...100 KM N OF SAL CABO VERDE
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 350 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1002 MB...29.59 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM CVT (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Gonzalo was
located near latitude 17.6 North, longitude 23.0 West. Gonzalo is
moving toward the north near 9 mph (15 km/h). A motion between 
north and north-northwest is expected to continue through the 
weekend, with a deceleration and a turn to the west-northwest 
expected early next week. On the forecast track, the center will 
continue to move away from northeastern portions of the Cabo
Verde Islands today.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Weakening is anticipated, and Gonzalo could become a remnant 
low or dissipate within the next 24 hours.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles (295 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1002 mb (29.59 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Gonzalo are expected to affect portions
of the Cabo Verde Islands through today before diminishing Sunday.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM CVT.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Tropical Storm Gonzalo Forecast Discussion Number 6
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026 
428 
WTNT42 KNHC 260848
TCDAT2
 
Tropical Storm Gonzalo Discussion Number   6
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL072026
800 AM CVT Sat Sep 26 2026
 
The convective structure of Gonzalo has not changed much during the 
last 6 hours.  It continues to be a sheared tropical cyclone, with 
the somewhat ill-defined low-level center exposed to the southwest 
of the convective mass due to 30 kt of southwesterly shear 
occurring over the cyclone.  The TAFB current intensity number is 
2.5/35 kt. Objective intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS range from 
34-41 kt. Based on these estimates as well as earlier scatterometer 
data, the intensity is held at 40 kt, but this could be a bit 
generous.

The initial motion is northward, or 350 degrees at 8 kt.  This 
general motion should continue for another day, followed by a 
deceleration and a turn toward the west-northwest by Monday.  The 
storm is already experiencing 30 kt of southwesterly vertical wind 
shear, and the shear is expected to increase to over 40 kt by hour 
12 of the forecast, so I expect the convection to continue moving 
farther away from the low-level center.  This should lead to Gonzalo 
becoming post-tropical by hour 24 or a bit sooner.  Model guidance 
is in good agreement that Gonzalo will weaken significantly over the 
next 36 hours, and the NHC forecast follows the guidance.  Earlier 
ASCAT data indicated the low-level circulation was becoming 
elongated.  If this trend continues, then Gonzalo could dissipate 
sooner than forecast.
